findings.message: PR uses threading.RLock instead of the threading.Lock specified in the issue; the choice is well-documented inline (reentrance from _get_jwt holding the lock across _fetch_authorized_integration_jwt) and is a strict superset, so no acceptance criterion is weakened.

tests.message: Concurrent-fetch tests assert urlopen.call_count == 1 but never verify that _JWT_CACHE holds the expected token afterward, leaving cache state under-tested for the changed code path.

No test exercises _fetch_authorized_integration_jwt raising while the lock is held, so exception propagation, lock release, and cache-not-written-on-error behavior of the new lock wrapper are untested.

The RLock choice (vs. Lock) is justified by reentrance from _get_jwt holding the lock across _fetch_authorized_integration_jwt, but no test would specifically fail if _JWT_LOCK were downgraded to a non-reentrant Lock with the inner 'with _JWT_LOCK' removed.
Race-window widening relies on a fixed 50 ms sleep in the mocked urlopen; on extremely contended CI the widening may be too short to deterministically expose a missing lock.

tests.message: The comment claims the test 'deterministically fails if the lock is removed', but no assertion-only-no-lock variant is kept in the suite to prove that claim holds for this race-condition test design.
No test exercises the error path where _fetch_authorized_integration_jwt raises while holding the lock; cache and lock state should remain consistent (not asserted).

The _JWT_LOCK is an RLock specifically so _fetch_authorized_integration_jwt can re-acquire it from inside _get_jwt; the suite has no nested-acquisition test that would catch a regression to a non-reentrant Lock (which would deadlock here).

Concurrency tests widen the race with time.sleep(0.05) inside the mocked urlopen; on heavily loaded CI the 10 threads may not actually overlap inside _fetch_authorized_integration_jwt, which could let a buggy implementation occasionally pass single-fetch assertions.
test_serial_cache_hit_no_fetch bundles three sub-scenarios (hit/miss/expiry) into a single test method; failures will not pinpoint which sub-scenario regressed.

TestJwtCacheConcurrency relies on a hardcoded time.sleep(0.05) in slow_urlopen to widen the race window; under variable CI scheduling the threads may serialize before the first fetch starts, deflating coverage of the contended path. Consider asserting the lock object identity/type or using a barrier that holds inside the mock.

No test asserts the RLock re-entrant contract (RLock → non-reentrant Lock regression would deadlock under _get_jwt→_fetch_authorized_integration_jwt) and no test covers the failure path where urlopen raises during the fetch (lock/cache invariants after a partial fetch are unverified).

tests.message: PR title/body describe a fail-closed fix in precheck.py around the @ai-reviewer dismiss permission check, but the diff shows concurrency changes in forgejo_backend.py with tests in test_forgejo_backend.py; no test in the diff covers the stated precheck fail-closed contract (e.g., returning an empty maintainer set on permission-check errors vs. raising/skipping).

TestJwtCacheConcurrency._run_concurrent_get_jwt relies on a hardcoded time.sleep(0.05) in slow_urlopen to widen the race window; this timing-dependent widen-the-race strategy can be flaky under variable CI scheduling (threads may serialize before the first fetch starts, deflating coverage of the actual contention).

No explicit test asserts the RLock re-entrant contract: _fetch_authorized_integration_jwt acquires _JWT_LOCK to publish the cache while _get_jwt already holds it across the fetch; the new tests exercise this only implicitly, and a regression to a non-reentrant Lock would not be caught by an isolated re-entrancy assertion.

No test covers the failure path in the token exchange (e.g., urlopen raising URLError or HTTPError); lock/cache invariants after a partial fetch are not asserted, so a regression that leaves _JWT_CACHE populated with a bad value or the lock held on exception would go undetected.
